Object: To DETERMINE THE ENTHALPY OF NEUTRALIZATION
OF A STRONG ACID AND A STRONG BASE

Enthalpy of neutralization of an acid (or a base) is defined as amount of heat released when 1 gm equivalent of the acid (or the base) is neutralized by 1 gm equivalent of a base (or an acid), both being in dilute SOIutions. The enthalpy of neutralization of a strong acid with a strong base is almost constant and is nearly equal to —13.7 K cals or — 56 KJ.
